shots.title: THE SHIP BEFORE THE DISASTER
shots.subtitle: Actual photograph • September 1911
shots.why: A genuine view of RMS Titanic establishes the vessel named by the opening and avoids fictional ship silhouettes.

shots.title: THE 1912 BRITISH INQUIRY
shots.subtitle: Period illustrated press record • May 1912
shots.why: Actual illustrated coverage of the exact British inquiry being cited by the narrator, not an invented report page.

shots.title: ACTUAL TITANIC LIFEBOAT · 1912
shots.subtitle: Real survivors after sinking • capacity from 1912 inquiry
shots.why: Directly relevant contemporaneous NARA photograph of an actual Titanic lifeboat provides real period visual for the narration of Titanic's boat capacity; the precise 1,178 rated capacity comes from the 1912 British inquiry, not inferred from this photograph.

shots.title: 14 + 2 + 4 BOATS
shots.subtitle: Original numerical explanation • British report
shots.why: No photograph can individually explain 14 standard + 2 emergency + 4 collapsible at one glance without inventing a count.

shots.title: 1,023 PEOPLE WITHOUT PLACES
shots.subtitle: Rated-capacity arithmetic • British report
shots.why: This difference is a derived number, so a sourced diagram conveys it precisely; photo of survivors cannot prove the arithmetic.

shots.title: REAL SURVIVORS, REAL LIFEBOAT
shots.subtitle: 15 April 1912 • approaching Carpathia
shots.why: Uses an authenticated lifeboat photograph only as concrete context for boats and their occupants after disaster; explicitly not proof of launch occupancy.

shots.title: CARPATHIA'S RESCUE
shots.subtitle: Actual 1912 photo • AFTER the sinking
shots.why: Rescue photos directly illuminate the limits of the rescue system without simulating fictitious launch footage.

shots.title: THE STORY CONTINUES
shots.subtitle: 1912 photographic record • Subscribe for evidence
shots.why: An actual rescue image anchors the closing invitation in human history rather than a meaningless generic subscribe slide.

shots.title: THE REAL TITANIC WRECK
shots.subtitle: Actual NOAA expedition photograph • 2003
shots.why: Actual original NOAA photograph of Titanic's in-situ wreck remains substantiates the wreck physically exists. The photographed rusticles are not represented as the port railing, the 1985 discovery, or 2024 expedition footage.

shots.title: 2024: THE MISSING RAILING
shots.subtitle: Illustration of the reported 15-foot port section • NOT 2024 footage
shots.why: Actual 2024 commercial expedition images are not released for commercial reuse; schematic is disclosed and grounded in the reported measurement.

shots.title: DIANA OF VERSAILLES
shots.subtitle: Illustrative silhouette • NOT a recovered-artifact photo
shots.why: Specific 2024 Diana expedition photographs are not proven commercially reusable; do not counterfeit them.

shots.title: THE WRECK CONTINUES TO CHANGE
shots.subtitle: Actual captain's bathroom • NOAA expedition archive
shots.why: Documented interior corrosion and rusticles in the actual Titanic bathroom are a distinct photograph from the opening and relevant proof of the physical deterioration studied by researchers. It is not a 2024 rail photograph.

shots.title: 2022 SURVEY → 2025 REVEAL
shots.subtitle: Source-timed timeline • no proprietary scan footage
shots.why: The relevant 2022/2025 Magellan/NatGeo scan is copyright-restricted; dated original infographic avoids republishing proprietary frames.

shots.title: REAL IMAGES. REAL EVIDENCE.
shots.subtitle: 2003 NOAA wreck record • not a 2024 image
shots.why: Return to a labelled detail of the genuine 2003 rusticles photograph for the narration 'Those images are new evidence' without pretending this archival image specifically shows 2024 damage; the image's source and date are disclosed.

shots.title: BUT IT CANNOT SHOW THE FINAL NIGHT
shots.subtitle: RMS Titanic • genuine 1911 photograph, NOT the sinking
shots.why: The ship before departure is an authentic dated photograph establishing what the wreck cannot recover: all details of the actual 1912 sinking. A distinct meaningful narrative beat.

shots.title: HISTORY IS STILL BEING STUDIED
shots.subtitle: Belfast shipbuilding • original period photograph
shots.why: A period shipyard image broadens the evidence context for concluding invitation and closing channel attribution.

rights_policy: Only exact individually named Commons assets with documented Public Domain metadata permitted in these 16 pictures, with returned author/license/hash; 2004 NOAA/IFE/URI image excluded. Remaining final subjective playback approval is separate.

real_shares.short_02: 5/8 authentic 1912+NOAA expedition photos, plus 3 original necessary diagrams

revised_visual_direction: Both Shorts reedited after rights audit. One formerly uncertain NOAA/IFE/URI 2004 bow photo REMOVED from all Short02 shots.
